title: Umbilical cord care: keep it dry and watch
summary: The stump usually dries and falls off on its own in one to three weeks.
whatsNormal:
The umbilical cord stump dries, darkens, and shrinks before it separates.

• Falls off on its own, usually between 1–3 weeks
• A small amount of dried blood or scab at the base is common
• Mild odor as it dries can happen; heavy odor is not normal
• Sponge baths only until the stump falls off and the belly button heals

Keep the stump dry: fold diapers below it, avoid submerging in bath water, and skip alcohol wipes unless your clinician recommends them.
watchFor: Redness spreading onto the skin around the belly button
Pus, continuous oozing, or foul smell from the stump
Baby fussy when you touch the belly area or feeds poorly
Stump still attached after 3 weeks, mention at the next visit
callDoctorIf: Bleeding that does not stop with gentle pressure for a few minutes
Red streaks on the belly or fever with cord redness
Swollen or bulging area after the stump falls off (possible hernia, usually not urgent but needs evaluation)
You see tissue growing over the stump (granuloma), often easy to treat in clinic
